discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 229051e. The writer now lives behind its own per-session mutex; terminal_write takes the sessions lock only to clone that handle, then releases it before the blocking write_all. kill and kill_all only need the sessions lock.

Fair, the per-session lock alone still let a blocked write_all stall the sync IPC command thread. 939760a moves the write off that thread entirely: each session now owns a writer thread fed by an unbounded mpsc channel, and terminal_write only enqueues. Dropping the session (kill/exit) drops the sender and the thread ends; a write blocked on a shell that stopped reading returns EIO once the shell is killed and the PTY closes. Verified live: a 200KB pipe plus kill stays responsive.

Good catch. The webview never reuses a tab id (each tab gets a fresh id and spawns at most once), so this was theoretical, but the defensive replace path made it reachable in principle. 69265482b tags each session with a generation and the reader only removes the entry if the map still holds its own generation.

Agreed, and fixed in ecd266455. A missing session bus or missing watcher is rejected immediately by the bus daemon itself (ENOENT / ServiceUnknown), so the only way to reach the 250 ms timeout is a watcher that exists but is slow to answer (a busy plasmashell or gnome-shell). Quitting there would end sessions on a desktop that does have a tray, while hiding there is just the pre-existing behavior. A timeout now keeps the hide-to-tray path, the doc comment explains why, and the test was flipped to `slow_probe_keeps_the_tray_behavior`.

Pushing back. The timeout has to resolve one way, and either direction is "wrong" for one of the two ambiguous cases, so the question is which mistake is cheaper.

For the timeout to fire with no host present, the bus daemon itself has to stall for more than 250 ms: a missing bus fails the connect immediately, and a missing watcher gets ServiceUnknown from dbus-daemon without consulting any other process. A stalled dbus-daemon is not a steady state on any desktop, and if it does happen the result is the pre-existing behavior, which relaunching recovers (the single-instance plugin re-shows the window).

For the timeout to fire with a host present, the watcher (plasmashell, or gnome-shell with the extension) just has to be busy for 250 ms, which is far more plausible. Quitting there ends running sessions on a desktop that has a working tray, and nothing recovers that.

So the timeout deliberately resolves toward hide (ecd266455, after the previous round flagged the other direction). The doc comment on `host_registered_within` records this reasoning.
